tagline: Through the smokeless coalfields, one company town after another.
intro: Out of Bluefield, US 52 works north through narrow valleys to Bramwell and Northfork and on to Welch, at the meeting of Tug Fork and Elkhorn Creek. There the trail turns onto WV 16, up through Mullens on the Guyandotte and Beckley toward Ansted. Small commercial districts line the valleys, and the houses climb the mountainsides above them.

This is the smokeless coal country. The mines brought people from many lands, and the companies built the towns and the company stores, with clubhouses and courthouses dressed by Italian stonemasons. Some of the mines have gone quiet. At Beckley an old mine opened to visitors in 1962.

moments.title: Bramwell
moments.text: In the late 1800s this little town on the Bluestone River was said to have more millionaires per head than anywhere in the country, and the coal operators built their big houses accordingly.

moments.title: Kimball
moments.text: The first memorial building raised for African-American veterans of the First World War stands in a town of 145, where the mayor is also the police force.

moments.title: Itmann
moments.text: Pocahontas Fuel opened a mine here in 1918 and named the town for its president, I. T. Mann, run together, and the town got a massive stone company store.

practical: The road is narrow and curving, with frequent speed changes through small towns and coal trucks to watch for. Some stretches are remote, with few services.
